jp: 誰[だれ]{が|ga-question}朝[あさ]ご飯[はん]{を|o-object}作[つく]ります{か|ka-question}。
en: Who makes breakfast?
why: A question word that is the subject is never marked with は; the unknown doer takes が.

jp: 何[なに]{が|ga-question}冷蔵庫[れいぞうこ]{に|ni-location}入[はい]っています{か|ka-question}。
en: What is in the fridge?
why: The unknown thing asked about with 何 is the subject, so it takes が rather than は.

jp: どの部屋[へや]{が|ga-question}お兄[にい]さん{の|no-possessive}部屋[へや]です{か|ka-question}。
en: Which room is your brother's?
why: どの picks one out of several unknown candidates, and that question-word subject takes が.

jp: 家族[かぞく]{の|no-possessive}中[なか]{で|de-scope}誰[だれ]{が|ga-question}一番[いちばん]早[はや]く起[お]きます{か|ka-question}。
en: Who gets up earliest in your family?
why: 誰 is the unknown subject of the question, so it must be marked with が.

jp: 今日[きょう]{は|wa-topic}誰[だれ]{が|ga-question}ごみ{を|o-object}出[だ]します{か|ka-question}。
en: Who is taking out the rubbish today?
why: The topic 今日 takes は, but the question word 誰 as the subject takes が.

jp: どちら{が|ga-question}お父[とう]さん{の|no-possessive}傘[かさ]です{か|ka-question}。
en: Which one is Father's umbrella?
why: どちら asks which of two, and a question word in subject position takes が.

jp: 誰[だれ]{が|ga-question}電話[でんわ]{に|ni-target}出[で]ます{か|ka-question}。
en: Who will answer the phone?
why: 誰 is the unknown person who will act, so it is the subject marked with が.

jp: どの犬[いぬ]{が|ga-question}あなた{の|no-possessive}犬[いぬ]です{か|ka-question}。
en: Which dog is yours?
why: どの犬 is a question phrase standing as the subject, so it takes が.

jp: 誰[だれ]{が|ga-question}ここ{に|ni-location}この花[はな]{を|o-object}置[お]きました{か|ka-question}。
en: Who put this flower here?
why: Asking who did something makes 誰 the subject, and it takes が.

jp: 誰[だれ]{が|ga-question}先[さき]にお風呂[ふろ]{に|ni-destination}入[はい]ります{か|ka-question}。
en: Who will take a bath first?
why: 誰 is the unknown subject, so が marks it; は cannot follow a question word like this.

jp: あ、台所[だいどころ]{で|de-place}お湯[ゆ]{が|ga-subject}わいています。
en: Oh, the water's boiling in the kitchen.
why: A new event you notice is reported with が; は would treat the water as already known.

jp: 隣[となり]{の|no-possessive}部屋[へや]{で|de-place}赤[あか]ちゃん{が|ga-subject}泣[な]いています。
en: A baby is crying in the next room.
why: Hearing a baby cry is a fresh happening, so the baby is introduced as the subject with が.

jp: 庭[にわ]{で|de-place}子供[こども]{が|ga-subject}遊[あそ]んでいます。
en: Children are playing in the garden.
why: The sentence simply reports what is happening, so the new subject takes が.

jp: ほら、ソファー{の|no-possessive}上[うえ]{で|de-place}猫[ねこ]{が|ga-subject}寝[ね]ています。
en: Look, a cat is sleeping on the sofa.
why: ほら points out something you have just noticed, and the newly noticed subject takes が.

jp: 朝[あさ]{から|kara-from}雨[あめ]{が|ga-subject}降[ふ]っています。
en: It has been raining since morning.
why: Weather happening in front of you is plain news, so 雨 takes が.

jp: 玄関[げんかん]{で|de-place}犬[いぬ]{が|ga-subject}鳴[な]いています。
en: A dog is barking at the front door.
why: A dog barking is a new sound you report, so the subject is marked with が.

jp: 机[つくえ]{の|no-possessive}上[うえ]{に|ni-location}手紙[てがみ]{が|ga-existence}あります。
en: There is a letter on the desk.
why: Saying that something exists in a place introduces it with が, not は.

jp: 庭[にわ]{に|ni-location}小[ちい]さい池[いけ]{が|ga-existence}あります。
en: There is a small pond in the garden.
why: A thing whose existence is being announced takes が; は would make it a contrast.

jp: うち{の|no-possessive}近[ちか]く{に|ni-location}パン屋[や]{が|ga-existence}あります{よ|yo-assertion}。
en: There is a bakery near our house.
why: You are telling the listener something exists, so the bakery is marked with が.

jp: 私[わたし]{の|no-possessive}部屋[へや]{に|ni-location}大[おお]きい窓[まど]{が|ga-existence}あります。
en: There is a big window in my room.
why: あります states that a window exists, and the thing that exists takes が.

jp: 祖母[そぼ]{の|no-possessive}家[いえ]{に|ni-location}猫[ねこ]{が|ga-existence}三匹[さんびき]います。
en: There are three cats at my grandmother's house.
why: います introduces living things that exist in a place, and they take が.

jp: 部屋[へや]{に|ni-location}大[おお]きい虫[むし]{が|ga-existence}います。
en: There is a big bug in the room.
why: A bug you have just found is newly introduced, so it takes が with います.

jp: 玄関[げんかん]{に|ni-location}知[し]らない靴[くつ]{が|ga-existence}あります。
en: There are some shoes I don't recognise at the front door.
why: Shoes you have just noticed are new information, so they take が with あります.

jp: 二階[にかい]{に|ni-location}部屋[へや]{が|ga-existence}三[みっ]つあります。
en: There are three rooms upstairs.
why: Stating how many rooms exist introduces them as new, so they take が.

jp: 家[いえ]{の|no-possessive}前[まえ]{に|ni-location}小[ちい]さい公園[こうえん]{が|ga-existence}あります。
en: There is a small park in front of our house.
why: The park is being introduced as something that exists there, so it takes が.

jp: 母[はは]{は|wa-topic}料理[りょうり]{が|ga-stative}上手[じょうず]です。
en: My mother is good at cooking.
why: 上手 takes the skill it describes with が; は would turn it into a contrast.

jp: 弟[おとうと]{は|wa-topic}野菜[やさい]{が|ga-stative}きらいです。
en: My younger brother dislikes vegetables.
why: Likes and dislikes mark the thing liked or disliked with が.

jp: うち{の|no-possessive}犬[いぬ]{は|wa-topic}散歩[さんぽ]{が|ga-stative}大好[だいす]きです。
en: Our dog loves walks.
why: 大好き is a feeling predicate, so what is loved takes が.

jp: 祖父[そふ]{は|wa-topic}耳[みみ]{が|ga-stative}遠[とお]いです。
en: My grandfather is hard of hearing.
why: The part of the body that is the issue takes が; the person is the topic with は.

jp: 祖母[そぼ]{は|wa-topic}歌[うた]{が|ga-stative}好[す]きです。
en: My grandmother likes singing.
why: 好き marks the thing liked with が, while the person who likes it is the topic.

jp: 兄[あに]{は|wa-topic}サッカー{が|ga-stative}大好[だいす]きです。
en: My older brother loves soccer.
why: The object of a strong liking takes が.

jp: 父[ちち]{は|wa-topic}英語[えいご]{が|ga-stative}よく分[わ]かります。
en: My father understands English well.
why: 分かる is a stative verb, so the thing understood takes が.

jp: うち{の|no-possessive}猫[ねこ]{は|wa-topic}魚[さかな]{が|ga-stative}好[す]きです。
en: Our cat likes fish.
why: 好き takes what is liked with が, and the cat is the topic.

jp: この時計[とけい]{は|wa-topic}祖父[そふ]{が|ga-subject}くれました。
en: My grandfather gave me this watch.
why: The watch is the topic and the giver already takes が; two が phrases cannot open the sentence.

jp: この料理[りょうり]{は|wa-topic}母[はは]{が|ga-subject}作[つく]りました。
en: Mother made this dish.
why: The object is brought forward as the topic with は while the doer keeps が.

jp: その部屋[へや]{は|wa-topic}弟[おとうと]{が|ga-subject}使[つか]っています。
en: My younger brother uses that room.
why: The room is the topic, so は marks it and the person using it keeps が.

jp: この写真[しゃしん]{は|wa-topic}姉[あね]{が|ga-subject}撮[と]りました。
en: My older sister took this photo.
why: The photo is the topic; が is kept for the person who took it.

jp: あの自転車[じてんしゃ]{は|wa-topic}兄[あに]{が|ga-subject}買[か]いました。
en: My older brother bought that bicycle.
why: The bicycle is made the topic with は, and the buyer takes が.

jp: 洗濯[せんたく]{は|wa-topic}いつも母[はは]{が|ga-subject}します。
en: Mother always does the laundry.
why: The task is the topic, so it takes は; the person who does it takes が.

jp: このケーキ{は|wa-topic}姉[あね]{が|ga-subject}焼[や]きました。
en: My older sister baked this cake.
why: The cake is the topic with は, and the baker is the new subject with が.

jp: あの花[はな]{は|wa-topic}祖母[そぼ]{が|ga-subject}育[そだ]てました。
en: My grandmother grew those flowers.
why: The flowers are the topic with は, and the grower takes が.

jp: お弁当[べんとう]{は|wa-topic}いつも父[ちち]{が|ga-subject}用意[ようい]します。
en: Father always prepares the packed lunches.
why: The lunches are the topic, so they take は; the one who prepares them takes が.

jp: ごみ{は|wa-topic}毎朝[まいあさ]兄[あに]{が|ga-subject}出[だ]します。
en: My older brother takes out the rubbish every morning.
why: The rubbish is the topic with は and the person doing it keeps が.

jp: 肉[にく]{は|wa-contrast}食[た]べます{が|ga-but}、魚[さかな]{は|wa-contrast}食[た]べません。
en: I eat meat, but I don't eat fish.
why: は sets fish against meat; が would make the fish the thing doing the eating.

jp: 朝[あさ]{は|wa-contrast}牛乳[ぎゅうにゅう]{を|o-object}飲[の]みます{が|ga-but}、夜[よる]{は|wa-contrast}お茶[ちゃ]{を|o-object}飲[の]みます。
en: I drink milk in the morning, but tea at night.
why: は contrasts night with morning; 夜が would make night itself drink the tea.

jp: 平日[へいじつ]{は|wa-contrast}六時[ろくじ]{に|ni-time}起[お]きます{が|ga-but}、日曜日[にちようび]{は|wa-contrast}十時[じゅうじ]{に|ni-time}起[お]きます。
en: I get up at six on weekdays, but at ten on Sundays.
why: は contrasts Sundays with weekdays; が cannot mark a day as the one who gets up.

jp: 土曜日[どようび]{は|wa-topic}会社[かいしゃ]{に/へ|ni-destination}行[い]きません。
en: I don't go to the office on Saturdays.
why: A day on which something happens or not is set as the topic with は, never が.

jp: 夜[よる]{は|wa-topic}あまりテレビ{を/は|o-object}見[み]ません。
en: I don't watch much TV at night.
why: 夜 is the time frame set as the topic with は; が would make night the one watching.

jp: 雨[あめ]{の|no-possessive}日[ひ]{は|wa-topic}洗濯[せんたく]{を/は|o-object}しません。
en: I don't do laundry on rainy days.
why: A time frame like 雨の日 is the topic of the sentence, so it takes は.

jp: 最近[さいきん]、朝[あさ]ご飯[はん]{は/を|wa-negative}食[た]べません。
en: Lately I don't eat breakfast.
why: は on the object of a negative verb stresses what is not done; が would be ungrammatical here.

jp: 母[はは]{が/の|ga-sub-clause}作[つく]った料理[りょうり]{は/が|wa-topic}おいしいです。
en: The food Mother made is delicious.
why: Inside a clause that modifies a noun, the subject is marked with が, not は.

jp: 雨[あめ]{が|ga-sub-clause}降[ふ]っている{ので|node-because}、今日[きょう]{は|wa-topic}家[いえ]{で|de-place}勉強[べんきょう]します。
en: Because it is raining, I will study at home today.
why: The subject of a reason clause takes が; は would wrongly turn the rain into a contrast.

jp: 妹[いもうと]{が/の|ga-sub-clause}好[す]きな料理[りょうり]{は|wa-topic}カレーです。
en: The dish my little sister likes is curry.
why: The subject inside the modifying clause 妹が好きな takes が.

jp: 祖母[そぼ]{が/の|ga-sub-clause}毎朝[まいあさ]歩[ある]く道[みち]{は/が|wa-topic}静[しず]かです。
en: The road my grandmother walks along every morning is quiet.
why: The doer of a verb inside a noun-modifying clause is marked with が.

jp: 兄[あに]{が/の|ga-sub-clause}使[つか]っている部屋[へや]{は/が|wa-topic}二階[にかい]{に|ni-location}あります。
en: The room my older brother uses is upstairs.
why: Inside the clause that describes 部屋, the subject 兄 takes が.

jp: 台所[だいどころ]{から|kara-source}いい匂[にお]い{が|ga-sense}します。
en: A nice smell is coming from the kitchen.
why: Smells and sounds that you perceive are marked with が after します.

jp: 隣[となり]{の|no-possessive}部屋[へや]{から|kara-source}音楽[おんがく]{が|ga-sense}聞[き]こえます。
en: I can hear music from the next room.
why: With 聞こえる, the sound that reaches your ears takes が.

jp: 窓[まど]{から|kara-from}庭[にわ]{が|ga-sense}見[み]えます。
en: You can see the garden from the window.
why: With 見える, the thing that comes into view takes が.

jp: 今日[きょう]{は|wa-topic}何曜日[なんようび]です{か|ka-question}。
en: What day of the week is it today?
why: 今日 is the known topic you ask about, so it takes は; the question word is the new part.

jp: 犬[いぬ]{は|wa-topic}何歳[なんさい]です{か|ka-question}。
en: How old is your dog?
why: The dog is the known topic being asked about, so は is used and が would be odd.

jp: お母[かあ]さん{は|wa-topic}どこ{に|ni-location}います{か|ka-question}。
en: Where is Mother?
why: Mother is the known topic you are asking about, so it takes は; the new item is どこ.

jp: 週末[しゅうまつ]{は|wa-topic}家族[かぞく]{と|to-with}公園[こうえん]{に/へ|ni-destination}行[い]きます。
en: On weekends I go to the park with my family.
why: A time frame like 週末 is set as the topic with は; が would make the weekend the one going.

jp: 夕方[ゆうがた]{は|wa-topic}母[はは]{と|to-with}買[か]い物[もの]{に|ni-purpose}行[い]きます。
en: In the evening I go shopping with Mother.
why: 夕方 is a time frame set as the topic with は, not the doer of the action.

jp: 今朝[けさ]{は|wa-topic}とても寒[さむ]かったです。
en: It was very cold this morning.
why: 今朝 sets the time frame as the topic with は and the rest comments on it.

jp: 昨日[きのう]{は|wa-topic}一日中[いちにちじゅう]家[いえ]{に|ni-location}いました。
en: Yesterday I was at home all day.
why: 昨日 is a time frame, so it is the topic with は, never the subject with が.

jp: 水曜日[すいようび]{は|wa-topic}妹[いもうと]{が|ga-subject}皿[さら]{を|o-object}洗[あら]います。
en: On Wednesdays my little sister washes the dishes.
why: The day is the topic with は, and the person who washes the dishes keeps が.
